one_line: Demonstrates how altering one facial feature changes the perception of others, promoting an AI facial preview tool.

hook.what_happens: A split-screen portrait of a woman is shown with the text 'This is the same face twice. One thing on it was changed.'
hook.why_it_works: Creates a visual puzzle that engages curiosity immediately.

shots.description: Split-screen portrait of a woman with subtle chin alteration.
Zoomed-in view highlighting the nose and chin areas with circular overlays.
Heatmap visualization showing pixel changes on the face.
Portrait with vertical measurement lines comparing nose and chin projection.
Second subject portrait demonstrating eyelid hooding effects.
First subject portrait divided into facial thirds.
Portrait with a geometric mesh grid overlay.
Text instructions on a dark background encouraging the viewer to try a physical test.
Close-up of eyes transitioning to a search bar CTA.

devices.used_for: Proving that only the chin changed, not the nose.

devices.name: measurement lines
devices.what_it_is: Vertical lines indicating the relative depth of nose and chin.

devices.name: search bar mockup
devices.used_for: Directing users to search for the product.

onscreen_text.text: This is the same face twice.
One thing on it was changed.
Almost everyone points at the nose.
Your eye reads a feature against everything around it.
This is every pixel that changed.
Almost none of them are on the nose.
It didn't shrink. The face caught up.
One. The nose and the chin are read as one line.
A chin that sits back leaves the nose out in front.
Bring the chin forward and the nose settles back.
Two. Another face. The lid and the eye.
Skin resting on the lashes closes the eye beneath it.
Lift the hood and the eye reads open.
The eye didn't grow. The cover moved.
Three. A face is read in thirds.
Move one boundary and all three change.
None of this tells you what to do.
It tells you why one feature can't answer it.
Faces are read whole. Not feature by feature.
Push your lower jaw forward a few millimetres.

1 Push your lower jaw forward.
2 A few millimetres. Hold it.
3 Now look at your nose.
So the question was never one feature.
It's what the whole face does when it moves.
See it on your own face first.

narrative_arc: Hook: Present a visual puzzle of a face with one changed feature.
Reveal: Show that the chin was changed, not the nose, using pixel data.
Explanation 1: Explain the relationship between nose and chin projection.
Explanation 2: Explain the relationship between eyelid hooding and eye size.
Explanation 3: Explain facial proportions in thirds.
Interactive Test: Ask the viewer to physically test the illusion themselves.
CTA: Introduce Refina AI to preview changes on their own face.

cta.what: Search 'Refina AI' to see facial previews on your own face.

subjects: Unnamed woman (Subject 1) - demonstrating chin and facial thirds changes
Unnamed woman (Subject 2) - demonstrating eyelid blepharoplasty changes
what_makes_it_work: Highly engaging visual illusion hook that immediately challenges the viewer's perception.
Scientific-looking data visualizations (heatmaps, grids) that build authority and trust.
An interactive physical experiment ('Try it now') that proves the concept in real-time.

animations.name: Before-After Slider Reveal
animations.what_moves: A vertical divider line sweeps across the face, revealing the post-procedure chin augmentation.
animations.purpose: Demonstrates subtle facial changes by comparing before and after states side-by-side.
animations.reusable_as: Comparing any before/after states like photo editing or cleaning results.

animations.name: Nose Highlight Circle
animations.what_moves: A circular outline draws around the nose area.
animations.purpose: Directs viewer attention to the nose to address common misconceptions about facial changes.
animations.reusable_as: Highlighting specific focal points in product demos or educational diagrams.

animations.name: Chin Highlight Oval
animations.what_moves: An oval outline draws around the chin area.
animations.purpose: Highlights the actual area of modification (the chin) to contrast with the nose.
animations.reusable_as: Emphasizing specific regions of interest in medical or technical videos.

animations.name: Pixel Change Heatmap
animations.what_moves: A glowing heatmap overlay fades in, showing pixel-level changes on the face.
animations.purpose: Visually proves that the chin, not the nose, was the only modified area.
animations.reusable_as: Visualizing data differences, motion detection, or image modifications.

animations.name: Proportion Dimension Lines
animations.what_moves: Vertical dimension lines with tick marks draw on next to the nose and chin.
animations.purpose: Illustrates the spatial relationship and proportions between facial features.
animations.reusable_as: Showing measurements, scale, or technical dimensions in product blueprints.

animations.name: Facial Thirds Grid
animations.what_moves: Horizontal division lines and vertical bar segments draw on to divide the face into thirds.
animations.purpose: Explains the aesthetic concept of facial thirds and balance.
animations.reusable_as: Grid overlays for design, photography rule-of-thirds, or architectural layouts.

animations.name: Facial Mesh Overlay
animations.what_moves: A geometric wireframe mesh draws onto the face.
animations.purpose: Represents AI facial analysis and holistic structural reading.
animations.reusable_as: Tech-themed overlays, face tracking simulations, or 3D modeling previews.

animations.name: Search Bar Type-In
animations.what_moves: A search bar fades in and text types out 'Refina AI'.
animations.purpose: Acts as a call-to-action directing users to search for the brand.
animations.reusable_as: Standard CTA for search-based discovery in marketing campaigns.

signature_moves: TrimPath for technical callouts and highlights
Geometric grid overlays to convey scientific analysis
animation_language_summary.how_things_enter: Elements draw on via stroke paths or fade in smoothly.
animation_language_summary.how_things_leave: Elements fade out or are replaced by hard cuts.
animation_language_summary.how_scenes_change: Hard cuts between different subjects and analytical diagrams.
animation_language_summary.what_stays_still: The subject's face remains centered and static as overlays animate on top.
animation_language_summary.rhythm: Deliberate and educational, matching the explanatory voiceover.

what_we_should_steal: Pixel Change Heatmap for showing precise visual differences
Facial Mesh Overlay for high-tech analytical branding
Proportion Dimension Lines for clean technical callouts
